served.stem: Apoptosis runs on a family of enzymes that sit in the cell at all times as inactive precursors and are switched on in a cascade once the decision to die is made. What type of enzyme are they, and how does the cascade work?
choices: Proteases, switched on by cleavage, initiator caspases activating executioner ones
Nucleases, activated by a calcium surge, which cut the plasma membrane into blebs
Phosphatases, activated by cytochrome c, which strip phosphate off the mitotic spindle
Kinases, activated by cyclin binding, which phosphorylate the nuclear lamins
Ligases, activated by ATP binding, which crosslink the cytoskeleton into a rigid mesh
served.bankWhy: Caspases are proteases, and the name is worth unpacking: they carry a cysteine in the active site and cut their targets after aspartate residues. They wait in the cytosol as inactive procaspases, which lets a cell commit to dying in seconds without having to make anything new. Initiator caspases are activated first and then cleave executioner caspases, which go on to cut hundreds of cell proteins. Cleaving is both how they get switched on and how they do their work.

answer.text: Proteases, switched on by cleavage, initiator caspases activating executioner ones
answer.line: Caspases are proteases. They wait as inactive precursors, and each active one cuts the next one on: initiators first, then executioners.

steps: Name the enzyme family: caspases are proteases that cut proteins after aspartate.
They sit ready as inactive procaspases. A cut switches each one on, so the cell can commit in seconds without making anything new.
Initiators, caspase-8 or 9, cut the executioners, caspase-3, 6 and 7, on. The executioners then cut hundreds of cell proteins.

choices.text: Proteases, switched on by cleavage, initiator caspases activating executioner ones
choices.note: Cutting is both how they switch on and how they work.

choices.text: Nucleases, activated by a calcium surge, which cut the plasma membrane into blebs
choices.note: A nuclease does chop DNA late in apoptosis, downstream of the caspases. A nuclease cannot cut a membrane.

choices.text: Phosphatases, activated by cytochrome c, which strip phosphate off the mitotic spindle
choices.note: Cytochrome c is part of apoptosis, but it switches on a protease cascade through caspase-9. Stripping phosphates off the spindle is not part of cell death.

choices.text: Kinases, activated by cyclin binding, which phosphorylate the nuclear lamins
choices.note: Cyclin-dependent kinases phosphorylate lamins to take the nuclear envelope apart for mitosis. A nearby process, not cell death.

choices.text: Ligases, activated by ATP binding, which crosslink the cytoskeleton into a rigid mesh
choices.note: Ligases join molecules. Apoptosis takes cell structures apart, the opposite job.

student.lockIt: Caspases are proteases switched on by cuts: initiators cut executioners on, and executioners take the cell apart.
